title: I Used the Model-Railroad Throttle Hours on the Chair Who Camped the Yard

parts.text: I booked throttle B at 2:47 p.m. and chair Dorr was already camped on the only tagged yard. The card said: BOOK THE THROTTLE. NINETY MINUTES. YARD WITH THE TAG. I was fifty-three, member, holding a tag. Dorr shrugged. "Chairs are the railroad." I photographed the card, the tag, and his consist on my yard. Then I asked for the layout log. At 2:53 the superintendent pinged why Dorr's name was on a camped yard. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The superintendent can see Dorr's consist on the tagged yard during my throttle hours.

social.video_title: The chair camped the only tagged model-railroad yard — Part 1/2
social.description: Model railroad, a throttle tag, a camped yard. I logged the consist. Would you have asked the superintendent?

parts.text: Dorr called it ops until the superintendent asked for the still. I printed the log, the card, and the photo. The consist moved. Dorr booked his own ninety and told the next chair ops were always about optics. Optics is a word chairs use when yards exist. Hours now have a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE YARD. I keep throttle B. Dorr brown-bags the jokes. The layout finally looks like a tag, not a camp. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Chairs are not the yard — Part 2/2
social.description: Layout log, moved consist, and a second line. Was ops ever my tag?
